experiments.title: To measure the conversion time of ADC

blocks.text: Study to measure the conversion time of ADC

CONVERSION TIME  
The time between the start and end of the conversion is known as the conversion time. The positive pulse on CONVST pin starts the conversion and when BUSY pin is high, it indicates that conversion is completed. We can measure the time between the two using DSO. Given conversion time of ADC: 1.6uS

1. Make the connection as shown in FIGURE-6.1. 
2. Give onboard analog input signal of 1 KHz to the ANALOG IN of 12 BIT ADC and then connect the probes of DSO to 
     the IC pins where we have the SOC and BUSY test points. 
3. Now observe the waveform on DSO, we can measure the conversion time using cursor of DSO. 
4. Bring one cursor at the falling edge of SOC and other cursor at the rising edge of BUSY pulse as shown in 
     FIGURE-6.2 
CONVERSION TIME OBSERVED: 1.520us 
5. The time between these two is the total conversion time.
BEL-ADA board, its power supply and DSO

LTC1278 is 500ksps, sampling 12-bit A/D converter which has conversion time of 1.6uS.By observing the values of give conversion time of IC and measured conversion time of IC we can conclude that both are nearly same.

experiments.title: To measure the resolution of ADC

blocks.text: Study to measure the resolution of ADC

The resolution of a n-bit analog-to-digital Converter (ADC) is a function of how many parts the maximum signal can be divided into. The formula to calculate resolution is 2n. For example, a 12 bit ADC has a resolution of 212 = 4,096. Therefore, our best resolution is 1 part out of 4,096, or 0.012% of the full scale. An ADC takes an analog signal and turns it into a binary number. Thus, each binary number from the ADC represents a certain voltage level. Resolution is the smallest input voltage change a digitizer can capture. Resolution can be expressed in bits (LSB), in proportions, or in percent of full scale.  Resolution limits the precision of a measurement. The higher the resolution (number of bits), the more precise the measurement. An 8-bit ADC divides the vertical range of the input amplifier into 256 discrete levels. With a vertical range of 5 V, the 8-bit ADC cannot ideally resolve voltage differences smaller than 19 mV. In comparison, a 12-bit ADC with 4096 discrete levels can ideally resolve voltage differences as small as 1.2mV 
RESOLUTION OF UNIPOLAR ADC  
For calculating resolution of 12 bits unipolar input analog voltage we have following formula: 
                 Resolution = 1/212 ×Vref 
Where Vref is the applied unipolar input voltage range and 12 is the no. of bits of ADC.

PROCEDURE:-
1. Make the connection as shown in FIGURE-7.1 in 12 BIT ADC Section, move the slider switch SW26 in unipolar   
     mode, remove the jumper J4. 
2. Give on board variable DC input voltage to the ANALOG IN of 12 BIT ADC and observe the equivalent digital output   
     voltage by connecting the output pins to the onboard OUTPUT LEDs. 
3. Take the difference of applied voltage when all LEDs are glowing (Vmax) and when all LEDs are off (Vmin). 
4. This will give the voltage range of ADC. 
     Vref= (Vmax-Vmin) 
     Vmin(observed)=0V 
     Vmax(observed)=4.99V 
     Vref=4.99V 
Resolution = 1/212 ×Vref=4.99/4096=0.0012V 

RESOLUTION OF BIPOLAR ADC 
For calculating the resolution of 12 bits bipolar input ADC we have following formul
Resolution = 1/212-1× V(ref)  
Where V(ref) is the difference between applied maximum and minimum bipolar input voltage to the ADC and 12-1 i.e. 11 is the number of bits of ADC and the 12th bit (MSB) indicates the sign of input voltage.0 indicates the positive input voltage and 1 indicates the negative input voltage.

PROCEDURE:-
1. Make the connection as shown in FIGURE-7.2, move the slider switch SW26 in bipolar mode, connect the jumper    
    J4. 
2. Give on board variable DC input voltage to the ANALOG IN of 12 BIT ADC and observe the equivalent digital output 
    voltage by connecting the output pins to the onboard OUTPUT LEDs. 
3. Observe the glowing of LEDs representing the bipolar analog equivalent digital output. Take the difference of 
    applied voltage when all LEDs are glowing (Vmax) except MSB and when only MSB is glowing (Vmin).This is V(ref). 
Vmin observed= -2.49V 
Vmax observed=+2.49V 
V(ref)=(Vmax-Vmin)=4.98 
Resolution = 1/212-1× V(ref)=4.98/4096=0.0012V
LTC1278 is a 12-bit ADC with 4096 discrete levels that can ideally resolve voltage differences as small as 1.2mV.12 bit ADC has more resolution that 8 bit ADC with the same reference voltage.
